author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Number of people allowed to stay for third year on holiday maker visa to be increased from 5,000 to 25,000 under revised plan

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The federal government is backpedaling on its plan to cut backpacker numbers following criticism from regional stakeholder groups who rely on the travellers for labour.

The Albanese government is expected on Tuesday to lift the proposed cap on third-year working holiday visas, boost regional work requirements and delay the start of a new ballot system.

Continue reading...
title: Labor announces policy backflip to allow more backpackers to work in regional Australia

author: Maanvi Singh
description:
NWS issues advisories for long stretches of the northern California coast, warning that waves can quickly overpower anyone nearby

The massive, 50-ft swells along California’s coast this weekend foretold an intense week of towering waves to come.

Officials from the National Weather Service (NWS) had issued advisories for long stretches of the California coast, warning people that erratic and unpredictable waves could quickly overpower anyone nearby. The highest waves – which reached 50ft to 60ft (15.24 to 18.29 meters) – cracked along the popular Mavericks surf spot in San Mateo county, south of San Francisco.

Continue reading...
title: California braces for more towering waves as powerful storms approach

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Under growing pressure to sell government’s strategy, treasurer says Myefo will ‘help ease immediate capacity pressures without putting growth at risk’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jim Chalmers has promised next month’s mid-year budget update “will cut enough, but not too much”, as he flagged “substantial savings” to help in the fight against inflation.

The treasurer has come under growing pressure to sell the government’s economic strategy after five interest rate hikes, and amid rising unemployment and cost-of-living pressures.
title: Mid-year budget update will ‘cut enough, but not too much’, Jim Chalmers says

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Outage at major airline comes just three days after FAA issued rare nationwide ground stop on all US flights

United ⁠Airlines said on ⁠Monday ⁠that it was ​experiencing ⁠a widespread system ⁠outage, just three days after the Federal ⁠Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop on all US flights.

“We’re ‌aware of the widespread system outage, ‌and our teams are working ​hard to get ⁠things back ​up and ​running ​as soon ​as possible,” ‌United ​said in a post ​on X, in which the airline also “sincerely apologized” to customers.

Continue reading...
title: United Airlines says it is working to fix ‘widespread’ system outage

author: Dara Kerr
description:
The lawsuit stems from an earlier incident where the tech company’s products hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face

California sued OpenAI on Monday, accusing the artificial intelligence titan of developing its technology without safety or the public’s interest in mind.

The lawsuit concerns an incident earlier this year where OpenAI agents – semi-autonomous AI software that can carry out digital actions on behalf of users – launched a cyber-attack into the open-source AI platform Hugging Face.

Continue reading...
title: California sues OpenAI over safety concerns after rogue agent hacking

author: Maya Yang
description:
The FBI is leading the investigation into the Biourja Renewables incident after it led to a temporary evacuation

Authorities investigating a bomb found recently at an ethanol production plant in Peoria, Illinois, have taken a suspect into custody, according to the mayor there.

The Peoria mayor, Rita Ali, told the Guardian on Monday that leadership at the BioUrja Renewables plant “have informed me that a suspect is in custody”.

Continue reading...
title: Suspect in custody after bomb found at Illinois ethanol plant

author: Associated Press
description:
Bank of America, Chase, US Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist were listed by users who have been experiencing issues

Customers reported difficulty accessing their online accounts at some major US banks on Monday.

The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began Friday and lasted for hours, which affected services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot and had serious repercussions all around the world. Also on Friday, ageing equipment led to a temporary grounding of all commercial airplanes in the US, sparking travel havoc.

Continue reading...
title: Customers report difficulty accessing online services at major US banks

author: Sam Levine
description:
The university will conduct a series of measures after a former student was gang-raped at a fraternity house two years ago

Cornell University is set to announce a “full review” of fraternities and sororities determining their future on campus after an alleged sexual assault there has brought scrutiny to the system at the Ivy League school.

University president Michael Kotlikoff announced the review on Monday in an update outlining several steps the institution has taken after a woman said she was gang raped at an on-campus fraternity’s house.

Continue reading...
title: Cornell announces full review of Greek life after scrutiny over sexual assault case

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Strategy of redeploying forces to try to relieve siege of Taiz and protect Aden comes as Islamist group makes steady gains

Saudi Arabia has been accused by anti-Houthi forces over its military strategy after its Yemeni allies withdrew troops from the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait, as well as pulled back forces from parts of Marib in the central part of the country.

The Saudi-backed government explained the repositioning by saying the strategic priority is to break the attritional siege on Taiz, Yemen’s third city and to protect Aden, the southern port city in which the Saudi-backed and UN-recognised government is now based.

Continue reading...
title: Saudi Arabia challenged by Yemeni allies over ceding ground to Houthis

author: Steven Morris
description:
Ex-marine John Perkins, who also killed himself, had been violent to Kathryn Perkins over 42-year marriage, Exeter inquests hear

A “controlling and violent” former Royal Marine who shot his wife dead after she told him she was leaving was allowed to keep two licensed shotguns despite police knowing he had a history of domestic abuse.

John Perkins shot Kathryn Perkins at their home in Devon with a double-barrelled shotgun before killing himself with his second weapon.

Continue reading...
title: Devon police renewed shotgun licence of known abuser who later killed his wife

author: Oliver Milman in Antalya
description:
Former vice-president at Cop31 urges lawmakers to rethink contentious bipartisan Baaja bill advanced by the US Senate

It would be a “serious mistake” to pass a contentious bipartisan bill to speed up energy projects and datacenters that has divided Democrats and environmentalists, Al Gore said.

The legislation, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (Baaja), will make it easier to build large infrastructure projects in the US, from oil and gas pipelines and datacenters to crucial clean energy components such as solar and wind power and transmission lines, scaling back environmental protections and legal challenges in order to do so.

Continue reading...
title: Passing bill to speed up gas projects and datacenters would be ‘serious mistake’, Al Gore says

author: Sam Levine
description:
Dan Koh, an incoming House representative and ex-Biden staffer, blasts Trump for blaming previous administration

Donald Trump’s efforts to blame Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage – and the resulting travel chaos – on Democrats are “absurd”, an incoming Democratic member of Congress said on Sunday.

The president remained largely silent and out of public view as air travel shut down on Friday, but on Sunday he emerged to issue a series of posts blaming the incident on the Biden administration.

Continue reading...
title: Democrat writes off Trump’s attempt to blame party for flight grounding as ‘absurd’

author: Lisa Cox and Penry Buckley
description:
Bill to authorise expansion at Mount Pleasant coalmine, subject to a landmark high court decision, will be debated this week

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A New South Wales government bill to increase coal production at a Hunter Valley coalmine creates a “serious corruption risk” for the state due to a clause that would give the resources minister “king-like” powers, the barrister and anti-corruption campaigner Geoffrey Watson says.

The state parliament will this week debate legislation to allow MACH Energy to increase coal production at the Mount Pleasant mi
title: Proposed NSW laws to allow coalmine to increase production pose ‘serious corruption risk’

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Brand reacted with ‘shock and dismay’ after products were also found in a ‘bargain bin inside a gas station’

  • Business live – latest updates

David Beckham’s company reacted with “shock and dismay” after discovering his branded fragrance range was on sale in petrol stations and in Poundland, court documents have revealed.

The former England football captain’s brand, DB Ventures, has launched a lawsuit against the distributor of the products, arguing it allowed them to be sold in stores that had not been agreed upon.

Continue reading...
title: Beckham firm sues after fragrance found for sale in Poundland

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Suspect named as Greene Da’monte Khiree

  • Drug smuggling carries life sentence in Nigeria

An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.

Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player it named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.

Continue reading...
title: US basketball player arrested with 75lb of marijuana at Nigerian airport, say authorities

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Researchers forced to scrap original studies as NIH rethinks grants not in ‘alignment’ with administration’s priorities

Dr Jade Pagkas-Bather received her first grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) in June 2025 – a milestone in any researcher’s career.

She planned to study basic income as a medical intervention: her randomized control trial would test whether monthly grants of $500-cash helped poor, HIV-positive young people in Chicago stick with treatment. Her hypothesis was as straightforward as it was cutting.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Orwellian’: HIV scientist’s ordeal lays bare Trump officials’ interference in grant-making

author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
description:
French actor apologises to two women he was convicted of assaulting on a film set in 2021

The French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set, and has for the first time apologised to the victims.

“I was found guilty. I hear it and I accept this conviction,” Depardieu, 77, said in a written statement. “I address my deep and sincere apologies to those who suffered.”

Continue reading...
title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Victim’s father, however, remains excommunicated for joining Anglican church after abuse was discovered

A Roman Catholic priest who pleaded guilty to sexually abusing an altar server in south-west Louisiana – before the church then controversially excommunicated the victim’s father – was released from a state prison over the weekend after having completed a seven-year sentence.

Michael Guidry’s release from the Dixon correctional institute coincidentally came as the father of victim Oliver Peyton recovered from a life-threatening bout with neuroinvasive West Nile virus, which the family chronicled on social media posts closely followed by their supporters.

Continue reading...
title: Catholic priest released from Louisiana prison after serving seven years for sexually abusing altar server

author: Ames Alexander of Floodlight
description:
Agency’s Aspect plane once was a key part of tracking toxic chemicals during disasters – why is it now often grounded?

When an ammonia leak outside a hotel in Weatherford, Oklahoma, injured 74 people last November, the federal government’s chemical-detection plane stayed on the ground. It also sat idle during a March fire at a Valero refinery in Port Arthur, Texas, and when blasts at a Toledo, Ohio, recycling plant killed two workers in August.

“Ten years ago, it would have gone to all of them,” said Mark Thomas, a former EPA official who managed the program for 18 years.

Continue
title: Flying blind: inside the decline of the EPA’s chemical-detection plane

author: Vivian Ho
description:
Donald Trump on Sunday blamed the Biden administration for the four-hour nationwide flight stoppage that led to thousands of canceled flights over the weekend. Plus: How Israel is using Amazon facial recognition to track Palestinians

Good morning.

A four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on Friday threw the entire weekend into chaos, with thousands of flights getting canceled and even more delays. While air travel is expected to even out again on Monday, nearly 2,000 ​flights within, into or out of the US on Sunday were canceled and more than 8,600 were delayed.

What’s the Trump administration saying? “I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash on Sunday.

What has Trump said? Donald Trump did not comment on the grou
title: First Thing: Trump administration blames travel chaos on former presidents and Congress

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
Leigh Ross, 39, charged with causing death by dangerous driving after BMW being pursued by police collided with another car

A man has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving after two people were killed when their car was hit by a vehicle being chased by police.

A 22-year-old man and 23-year-old woman, both from York, died when their car was struck by a BMW being pursued by police in Leeds in the early hours of Sunday.

Continue reading...
title: Man charged after two people die in Leeds police pursuit crash

author: Tom McIlroy in Manila
description:
Quad leaders’ summit in Philippines is Trump’s first, as Australia joins US and Japan to protect AI technologies in face of China efforts to dominate

Anthony Albanese will attempt to walk a tightrope in his relationship with Donald Trump when the pair meets on Tuesday, arguing for a speedy resolution to the wars in Iran and Ukraine while urging the US to engage in the Indo-Pacific.

The Quad leaders’ summit in the Philippines’ capital of Manila will be Trump’s first, in either of his presidencies. The US president, fresh from a crushing midterms result, will take centre stage in gatherings of Asian leaders and prepare for historic three-way talks with Xi Jinping of China and Russia’s Vladimir Putin this week.
title: Albanese treads tightrope in upcoming Trump meeting, wanting Indo-Pacific engagement and end to Iran and Ukraine wars

author: Penry Buckley NSW state reporter
description:
Backdown is one of several premier Chris Minns has announced in recent weeks as state prepares for election in March

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Minns government has mothballed laws intended to protect homebuyers from underquoting after the premier said real estate agents in his Sydney electorate had raised concerns about their effect amid a housing market downturn.

Changes due to come into effect on Tuesday would have banned agents in New South Wales from lowering the advertised price of a property beneath a written offer previously rejected by a seller, with fines of up to $110,000 or three times an agent’s commission, whichever was greater.
title: NSW halts new law to crack down on underquoting by real estate agents at 11th hour

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: From situationship to a possible makeup, a look at the evolving relationship, and the bloc’s big feelings about the future

Good morning. Ahead of the hotly anticipated UK-EU summit this Friday, Andy Burnham is expected to make the reset of our relationship with Europe the pivotal theme of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet in London tonight.

The prospect of closer ties – and the possibility of going “all the way” to reversing Brexit – has been met with jubilation and relief in some quarters and vehement opposition in others, while around Westminster and across the media the psychodrama has been spiralling for weeks.

UK news | A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to campaign for a staggered age of c
title: Monday briefing: The many stages of the UK-EU relationship – and what’s next

author: Richard Adams and Sally Weale
description:
Planned reforms could include appeals to ombudsman or review panel for parents dissatisfied with provisions

Families of children with special needs may get new avenues to appeal for extra support at school, under major concessions being considered for the government’s overhaul of special needs education in England.

The move comes as the government’s reforms are being repeatedly criticised by campaigners and parents’ groups for watering down legal protections allowing families to appeal through a high court tribunal for support.

Continue reading...
title: Special needs overhaul in England could bring in new avenues for extra support

author: Nick Visser
description:
Students left in limbo after digital platform fails during exams, with university saying ‘third-party technical partners’ likely to blame for issue

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Hundreds of students at the University of Melbourne were forced to abandon their final exams on Monday morning after many were unable to access the digital platform needed to begin them.

Jol Scobie, a first-year student at the university, was set to take his Australian politics exam on Monday after preparing for weeks. He had initially been told earlier in the year it was going to be a hand-written essay before instructors changed the test to a digital platform.
title: Tech failure forces hundreds of University of Melbourne students to abandon final exams mid-test

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
New National Health and Medical Research Council guidelines at odds with public hospital bans in Queensland and NT

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s largest medical research organisation has advised puberty blockers are appropriate for the gender-affirming care of children in certain circumstances, after a year-long review of international evidence.

The federal government last year commissioned the commonwealth-funded National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) to develop the advice in response to bans in Queensland and Northern Territory
title: Australia’s national medical research body advises conditional use of puberty blockers for transgender children

author: Luca Ittimani and Associated Press
description:
Company insists Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese spy, left business in late 2025

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of the Nvidia chief, Jensen Huang, says it is a “legitimate and lawful business” and has announced that its director, who allegedly had an affair with Jensen Huang, left the business in late 2025.

The Singapore-based cloud computing company on the weekend said it was “aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence”.
title: Megaspeed, the company linked to the downfall of Nvidia boss, says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Supermarket giant says no customer, team or supplier data breached in cyber-attack but recommends customers update passwords

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s second-largest retailer has been targeted in a cyber-attack, though it is still too early to tell whether any of its data has been stolen or compromised.

Coles revealed the threat on Monday morning, saying it was investigating the incident with support from the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global security experts.

Continue reading...
title: Coles investigating ‘cybersecurity incident’ and apologises to customers
